about: Tennis's earlier seasons (docs/design/tennis.md, "Earlier seasons"): Tennis Abstract's own year-end Elo reports for 2016-2025, archived by the Wayback Machine, and year-end Elo computed from Jeff Sackmann's ATP match results by Tennis Abstract's published method for 1973-2015; 1960-1972 from a second run of the same method warmed up on his file of the amateur era's majors and Davis Cup (method.early). npm run sync:tennis-seasons rebuilds scripts/data/tennis-seasons/ from the pinned inputs (cached in the ignored data-src/tennis-seasons/); npm run build:tennis-seasons builds the season files from there.

reports.label: Tennis Abstract Elo, through the ATP Finals
reports.note: Tennis Abstract did not update the report again in 2017 (the capture of 28 November is the same file): the list stops at the ATP Finals and never took in the Davis Cup final.

sources: https://www.tennisabstract.com/blog/2019/12/03/an-introduction-to-tennis-elo/ (expected score; starts in the low 1200s since challengers and qualifying were added, depending on the level)
https://www.tennisabstract.com/blog/2018/05/15/handling-injuries-and-absences/ (layoff penalty, K after a layoff, second layoffs, the 1900 study population, the offseason not counted)
K = 250 / (matches + 5)^0.4 is FiveThirtyEight's formula, which Sackmann said he adapted (sleepomeno/tennis_atp examples/elo.R); his own worked example and the February 2016 report fit an offset of 6

start.fit: Not published: fitted on Tennis Abstract's own current-method numbers for 1974-2000, the 23 career peaks of its Tennis 128 profiles and the 18 yElo seasons of its season tables (counted by the match files' seasons): mean difference -2.0 Elo, root mean square 15.1 (1970s -1.2, 1980s -1.6, 1990s -4.7).

layoff.note: A layoff of eight weeks or more between counted matches, 15 November to 15 January not counted, costs 100 points rising linearly to 150 at a year; K is then 1.5 times as large, back to normal over 20 matches; a second layoff within two years of the last comeback is charged the difference between the penalty for both together and for the first. Charged on return; a list shows a player in the middle of one with the penalty he would be charged on the list's date. Only for players rated 1900 or more, as in the study that set it (applied to everyone it lowers the whole list by 100 to 200 points against every published number).

method.counted: Tour-level main draws with the Davis Cup (atp_matches_<year>.csv), tour-level qualifying and challengers' main draws (atp_matches_qual_chall_<year>.csv), as Tennis Abstract's report says ("tour-level, tour-level qualifying, men's challenger"): not a challenger's qualifying (the files hold whole qualifying draws in 2018 and from 2022; counting them lists some 180 men a season Tennis Abstract does not and lifts the modern lists by 20 to 40 points), nor a walkover, retirement, default, abandoned or unfinished match, nor one without a score or against a placeholder opponent ("U Unknown").
method.order: By the files' season, then the event's date, the event, the round (qualifying first) and the match number: a season ends after its last event (the Masters played in January 1978-1986 belongs to the year before) and before the next season's first, even one that starts on 29 December.
method.activityNote: A season lists the men who played at least 10 counted matches in it, as Tennis Abstract's report has listed those with 10 in the last 52 weeks since 2020. The published seasons keep the men of Tennis Abstract's list who pass the same test in the match files.
method.asOf: A list is dated 31 December, or the start of the season's last event when that is later.

peaks.source: Tennis Abstract, The Tennis 128 (2022): each player's peak Elo by the current method, from his profile

yElo.source: https://www.tennisabstract.com/blog/2024/11/28/how-does-jannik-sinners-season-stack-up/ (the best seasons by yElo, Tennis Abstract's current method)

v1.note: Tennis Abstract's method before May 2018, for the check against its 2016 and 2017 reports: tour-level matches only, everyone starting at 1500, no layoff penalty.

early.about: The men's seasons before 1973 (docs/design/tennis.md, "Before 1973"): a second run of this method, kept apart from the first so that 1973-2025 rebuild byte for byte. It reads Sackmann's file of the amateur era (the majors and the Davis Cup, 1877-1967) before the open era's files, with the amateur file's duplicate ids merged, its newcomers starting at their own level and its layoffs charged only from 26 weeks, and snapshots 1960-1972 (seasons.early). The rest is the method above.
early.fileNote: 25,001 rows of two levels, the majors (G, 20,201) and the Davis Cup rubbers (D, 4,800); each row stops after 40 of the header's 49 cells (the empty statistics and rank cells left off, padded when read), and two rounds appear that the open era's files lack: PR, a preliminary round before the first full one, and CR, the challenge round of Wimbledon to 1921 and of the US Championships to 1911. A row's season is the year of its date. Every row is counted but walkovers, retirements, defaults and placeholder opponents.

start.fit: Not published: a newcomer whose first counted match is in the amateur file starts at 1360, fitted to five points so that the run carries on as the shipped one. On Tennis Abstract's 38 targets for 1973-2000 (targets above) it comes out 2.0 Elo low on average, root mean square 15.3 (the shipped run: 2.0 and 15.1), and over the shipped run's top 50 of each season 1973-1980 its Elo of the same men differs from the shipped run's by 0.4 to 3.0 points on average (absolute), by -1.2 to +2.6 in all. A start of 1350 leaves those seasons 0.1 to 4.8 points under the shipped run, 1370 2.9 to 5.9 over it, 1450 (the open era's tour start) 18 to 30 over it.

layoff.note: The open era's rule (layoff above) for every gap that begins on or after 1 January 1968. A gap that begins and ends before it is charged on the same scale only when it lasts 26 weeks or more: the file holds about a third of a leading amateur's matches, so the eight-week rule charges nearly every amateur (against Tingay's top tens of 1960-1967, checks below, the mean rank correlation is 0.66 with eight weeks, 0.64 with 13, 0.70 with 26, 0.67 with 39 and 0.67 with no charge at all). A gap across the start, a professional coming back to the open events of 1968, is never charged.

activity.note: 1960-1967 (seasons.amateur) list the men with three counted matches in the season, 1968-1972 ten, as from 1973. The amateur file holds only the majors and the Davis Cup, about a third of a leading amateur's matches: a floor of ten would leave six to eight nations a season (and share 7.6 of Tingay's ten, rank correlation 0.78), five 15 to 20 (7.4, 0.74), three 23 to 30 (7.1, 0.70).

aliases.note: Duplicate ids, each merged into the id of the same man before rating (and so for his Davis Cup nations too), reviewed by hand on 2026-11-09. Two kinds: 'davis-cup', an id of the amateur file with Davis Cup rows only, joined to his id with majors or open-era rows; and 'open-era', an amateur id of a man who carries on in the open era under another one. Both share a country, and careers no more than two seasons apart unless the birth dates agree. Rules: 'name', the same full name; 'initial', the same surname and first initial; 'born', the same surname and birth date; 'hand', the same surname with a variant of the first name, accepted by hand. Of the two, the id the open era's files use is kept (the one with more open-era rows when both have some), else the majors id. No merged pair played the same event. Not merged: men of one surname told apart by their first names or birth dates (Constantin and Ilie Nastase, the Ulrichs, the Frasers, Vo Van Bay and Vo Van Thanh, whose surname is Vo), two ids in one event (always two men), and pairs with no evidence beyond the surname (Aragon, Mohan, Kirby, Reyes, Tapia, Cameron, Guimaraes, Badreldin and El Sayed, Sturdza). The player file's birth dates differ within 39 merged pairs by a day, a month, a year or a placeholder (1 January); their names, country and years agree.

nations.note: A computed season's player plays for the nation he played the Davis Cup for in the nearest season (the same season first, then earlier, then later, within six seasons), from the ties' names in the match files ("Davis Cup WG F: USA vs AUS"), else for his country by the player file, which gives only his latest; then as the state of that season knew it. A published season's player plays for the country Tennis Abstract's rankings report of the nearest date files him under, else for his country by the player file.

barred.name: South Africa
barred.why: Ejected from the 1970 Davis Cup over apartheid and banned indefinitely (Wikipedia, 'Sporting boycott of South Africa during the apartheid era', revision 1384419132): the match files have no South African tie in 1970-1972, and have them in 1968, 1969 and again from 1973.

barred.name: South Africa
barred.why: Barred over apartheid: the match files have no South African Davis Cup tie from 1979 until Group II in 1993 (they hold the World Group, Group I and Group II only).

barred.name: FR Yugoslavia
barred.why: Barred by the United Nations sanctions: the match files have no Yugoslav tie from February 1992 until Group II in 1996.

fixes.name: Jaroslav Drobny
fixes.why: Czechoslovak until 1950, Egyptian 1950-1959, British after 1959 (Wikipedia, 'Jaroslav Drobný', revision 1366019764); the player file lists him as Czechoslovak and his Davis Cup rows end with Czechoslovakia in 1949, so the nearest-season rule would keep him Czechoslovak.

fixes.name: Martin Mulligan
fixes.why: Australian until he played for Italy, 1968-1975 (Wikipedia, 'Martin Mulligan', revision 1381941027: a member of the 1968 Italian Davis Cup team); his only Davis Cup rows are Italy's of 1968, so the nearest-season rule would make him Italian from 1962.

fixes.name: Bob Hewitt
fixes.why: Australian until he became a South African citizen in 1967, after marrying a South African (Wikipedia, 'Bob Hewitt', revision 1383230922); his Davis Cup rows are South Africa's from 1967 and the player file lists him as South African, so he would be South African in every season before.

fixes.name: Johan Kriek
fixes.why: South African until he became an American in 1982; the player file lists him as American and he played no Davis Cup.

fixes.name: Kevin Curren
fixes.why: South African until he became an American in 1985; the player file lists him as American and he played no Davis Cup before.

fixes.name: Greg Rusedski
fixes.why: Canadian until he chose Great Britain in 1995; the player file lists him as British and his Davis Cup rows start with Great Britain in 1995.

fixes.name: Mikhail Kukushkin
fixes.why: Russian until he chose Kazakhstan in 2008, the year his Kazakh Davis Cup rows start.

fixes.why: Russian until he chose Kazakhstan in 2008, the year his Kazakh Davis Cup rows start.
